frames.observation: The exact custom bear is fully readable in settled native bear_idle. Its dark brown faceted body, golden back, rounded muzzle and small round eyes form a coherent low-poly silhouette with all four limbs planted.
A later bear_idle sample preserves the compact quadruped stance, face alignment, paw placement and golden shoulder-to-back panel without visible stretching, detachment or renderer loss.
At the native Attack transition into bear_attackBite, the bear lifts forward as one connected body. The face, torso and four limbs remain proportionate while the native glow overlaps the underside.

Late bear_attackBite keeps the head, shoulders, back and paws coherent during the forward airborne pose. The native 32-damage response and effects concern the hero and do not obscure the bear's main silhouette.
The ordinary zero-focus attack begins with Honeyback intact at HP72 in settled bear_idle. Face, torso and paws remain readable before the native player action resolves.
A second pre-impact sample preserves the same compact idle silhouette and exact custom material. This frame precedes the measured HP transition and does not by itself establish hit motion.

The telemetry-selected native Damaged trigger coincides with a bright impact sphere and foreground hero. The bear's face and upper silhouette remain aligned behind them, while the effect prevents fine inspection of the lower body.

The recorded 8-damage label is visible during native bear_damage. Honeyback rears into the hit pose with its head, torso, forelegs and golden back connected; the foreground hero blocks part of the lower chest.
After the ordinary damage reaction, Honeyback has recovered its quadruped idle at HP64. Camera afterimages soften the edges, but the face, back and four-limb stance retain their intended proportions.

The capture ends during native bear_attackPound after a complete bear_attackSwipe earlier in the sequence. The forward body, face and planted forelimbs remain coherent while a bright native effect overlaps the underside and hero.

The explicit KillSingle capture begins with the exact custom bear intact at HP64 in native bear_idle. The attack-selection UI is present, but this action is a separate fixture rather than ordinary lethal gameplay.

At the telemetry-selected native Death trigger, Honeyback remains aligned behind the foreground hero and large impact effect. The face is readable, but the glow prevents a detailed whole-body judgment at this instant.

Native bear_deathHeavy is underway with the recorded 1000-damage label. The connected bear rises into the heavy-death pose with limbs, torso and back moving together; this is an animated death rather than ragdoll behavior.

Honeyback reaches a coherent prone bear_deathHeavy pose with its face forward, body grounded and limbs spread. No visible mesh explosion, detached part or long deformation appears in this sampled resting pose.
A later unobscured sample preserves the same coherent prone pose and readable face. It establishes short sampled persistence inside this capture, not general corpse lifetime or cleanup behavior.

The native loot panel and foreground hero obscure most of the resting bear. A limb remains visible at the panel edge and exact telemetry is stable, but this image cannot establish full corpse appearance or cleanup.

At the end of the complete 120-frame capture, the loot panel still blocks most of the target area while part of Honeyback remains visible behind it. This handoff does not establish later corpse lifetime, cleanup causality or final disposal.

requirements: All 17 referenced original PNGs were inspected before assigning the reviewed status.
Every observation is scoped to the exact frame and its telemetry boundary.
The ordinary 72 to 64 hit is separate from the explicit 64 to 0 KillSingle fixture.
The source reports m_DoRagdoll false and zero rigidbodies, so bear_deathHeavy is animated and receives no ragdoll credit.

Exact renderer instance, owner, CEL, mesh and bone signature remain unchanged while active, enabled and reported visible in all 360 retained telemetry frames; exact collision, general corpse lifetime and final cleanup remain unproven.
